concerns.text: T000 violates Constitution Principle II (Verified Accuracy) by hardcoding 'Primary Source Truth' (DOI/Title) within the task logic instead of fetching/verifying against an external registry or primary source. This creates a semantic weakening of the 'Verified Accuracy' requirement, as the task cannot actually validate the citation against the real world, only against a hardcoded string.

T000b violates Constitution Principle II (Verified Accuracy) by hardcoding a specific 12-item list as 'Primary Source Truth' for Lee & See (2004). The task description admits these are an 'interpretation' or 'adaptation' rather than verbatim text. Hardcoding unverified text as the canonical source for the experiment violates the requirement that scale items be verified against the primary source before use.

T009 violates the semantic intent of a data contract (SC-004) by requiring the schema to be populated with 'verbatim text' of survey questions as field keys (e.g., `trust_item_1` containing the full question string). This conflates the data schema (structure/types) with the survey content (values), creating a structural violation that breaks downstream data parsing and violates the 'Single Source of Truth' principle for data contracts.

T038 creates a circular dependency that violates the 'Strict Sequence' constraint of the plan. It requires verifying `config.yaml` ranges against `docs/protocol.md`, but `docs/protocol.md` is generated by T042 (Phase 6), while T038 is in Phase 5. This makes the verification step impossible to execute as defined, violating the requirement for a valid execution order.

T008 requires `sensitivity_config` ranges to be 'justified in `docs/protocol.md`', but `docs/protocol.md` is not generated until T042 (Phase 6). This forces the Phase 0 configuration task to rely on a document that does not yet exist, violating the logical flow and the requirement for pre-registered justification before configuration.
